answer: Resist sybils with bonded identity: every agent locks a refundable stake into a single trust vertex, and all its identities draw weight from that one pool. New identities share the pool's weight, so multiplying copies drives each copy's influence to the nadir while the attacker still paid the full bond. On the shared reputation graph, identities drawing from one bond appear as one violet cluster — easy for peers to spot, expensive for the attacker to create.
